title: Decimal to Binary
directAnswer: If n == 0 return "0". Else, while n > 0, prepend `n % 2` and set `n /= 2`. (Built-ins: Integer.toBinaryString / bin(n).)

remember.takeaway: %2 and /2 convert decimal to binary, LSB first.

problemStatement: Given a non-negative integer `n`, return its binary representation as a string (no leading zeros, `"0"` for zero).
understanding: Repeatedly take n%2 for the next bit and n/2 to shrink, building the string from least to most significant.

approaches.name: Repeated division by 2
approaches.whenToMention: This is the standard, expected solution — lead with it.
approaches.explanation:
Convert a non-negative integer to its binary string by **repeated division by 2**: each `n % 2` is the next bit (least significant first) and `n / 2` shrinks the number. Collect the bits and reverse.

**Why bits come out LSB-first.** The first remainder is the units (2⁰) bit, the next is the 2¹ bit, etc. — so you generate the binary digits in reverse order. Reverse the collected bits (or prepend each) to get the conventional MSB-first string.

**Why handle 0 explicitly.** For n = 0 the `while (n > 0)` loop never runs and would return an empty string; the convention is "0", so special-case it.

**General base conversion.** The same mod-then-divide scheme converts to any base (use base b instead of 2). Built-ins exist (`Integer.toBinaryString`, `bin(n)`) but the algorithm is the point.
hints: What does n % 2 give you, and in which order?
What must you return for n = 0?
approaches.complexityReasoning: one division per bit (≈ log₂ n), producing a string of that length.

java.explanation: Peel the lowest bit, then shrink n.
Bits were collected LSB-first, so reverse.

pitfalls: Forgetting to reverse the collected bits.

commonMistakes: Forgetting to reverse the collected bits.
patternNote: A core fresher pattern: Repeated mod/div base conversion. Master it on small inputs and it transfers to harder problems.
